claims.head: Blackwood doesn’t own the Flames
claims.body: Blackwood has been a wall against the Flames since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Blackwood isn’t that wall tonight.

claims.head: Who drives the play: the Avalanche
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Avalanche have been the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Flames one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Avalanche’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

CGY.head: The Avalanche should be favored
CGY.body: Even though Colorado is on the second night of a back-to-back and Calgary has home-ice advantage, the Avalanche have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames’ best hope is piling up shots, plus a big night in goal.

COL.head: The Avalanche should be in control
COL.body: Even though Colorado is on the second night of a back-to-back and Calgary has home-ice advantage, the Avalanche have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. If the Flames want to spoil it, start with piling up shots.

story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Flames are still looking for their first win of the season, 0-3-0 through three games. The Avalanche are 2-1-0.

It’s strength against strength: the Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Avalanche are near the top at keeping shots away. Don’t read much into Blackwood’s record against the Flames.

items.text: The Flames are newly without Joel Hanley, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season.
Nathan MacKinnon has a point in four straight games against Calgary, with a goal in each of the last three, and 17 points in his last nine against them.
Nazem Kadri faces his old team, Calgary.
